targets.notes: On a tokenize of about 4000 distinct dictionary headwords, cProfile shows Matcher._run as the largest self-time cost on the lookup path: about 0.26s of 1.27s, across 32664 calls. Even on repeated text, where the arc cache is hot, it is still about 0.21s of self time. The time is the pure-Python common-prefix walk. Each call probes every prefix from 8 bytes downward in an OrderedDict, and on a hit takes a lock, deletes that entry, and stores a fresh copy of the output set. The walk then steps arc by arc and builds outputs with bytes concatenation. A prefix index that does not slice and copy on every byte, plus fewer copies of the output set, can return the same set of outputs with less work.

Matcher._run calls next_arc once per arc. On repeated text the 4096-slot cache absorbs this, but on the same varied tokenize the cache sits at its cap and next_arc itself shows about 0.15s of self time across 141715 calls, with far more misses than the cache can hold. Each miss reads a flag byte, several struct integers, and output slices from the compiled FST and returns a new 6-tuple. Parsing those fields with fewer allocations, or keeping a denser decoded form of the arcs, would return the same tuples. The benchmark cycles more distinct arc addresses than the cache, so it measures that miss path.
